# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Rowan Novak**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** Healthy Blue Louisiana — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-16**
- **Member:** Rowan Novak
- **Member ID:** W671638429
- **Reference number:** POC-7CD7D16B79-75735
- **Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
- **Plan:** Healthy Blue Louisiana (Commercial/ACA), Louisiana
- **Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) that my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has requested and documented as medically necessary. The notice dated 2026-08-16 states that the records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records that were submitted do document conservative treatment, and they line up directly with the plan's own published criteria in Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1).

Below I have set out the plan's criteria in its own words, followed by what is in my medical records.

## 1. The length of my conservative treatment

The policy states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"

My records show supervised physical therapy from 2026-03-22 to 2026-06-28 — **14 weeks, with 20 visits completed** — focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is longer than the 12 weeks the policy names.

In addition, my MRI of 2026-06-20 describes **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4** changes medially. Grade 4 is the exact circumstance the policy's own parenthetical identifies as an exception to the 12-week requirement. I meet the criterion both ways.

## 2. What conservative treatment had to include

The policy states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

On physical therapy, the policy states:

> "Physical therapy requirement includes ANY of the following: Physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider of physical therapy services Supervised home treatment program that includes ALL the following: Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

My therapy was **supervised physical therapy**, which satisfies the first listed option.

On the complementary treatment, the policy states:

> "Complementary conservative treatment requirement includes ANY of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Intra-articular corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

My records document **two** of these, not just the one the policy requires:
- **NSAIDs for 4 months**, with inadequate relief; and
- an **intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-07**, which gave only about two weeks of partial relief.

## 3. Why the conservative treatment is considered to have failed

The policy states:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

Each part is in my chart:
- **Full course completed:** 20 physical therapy visits over 14 weeks, completed and discharged on 2026-06-28; 4 months of NSAIDs; one corticosteroid injection.
- **No significant improvement:** my pain has been progressive over **18 months** and is **unrelieved by rest**. The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief and the injection gave only two weeks of partial relief. On examination there is positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- **More invasive therapy being considered:** that is exactly what this request is — the partial knee replacement Dr. Okafor has recommended.

## 4. Documentation of duration, severity and function

The policy states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

And on severity, the policy states:

> "Reporting symptom severity – Severity of pain and its associated impact on activities of daily living (ADLs) and instrumental ADLs (IADLs) are key factors in determining the need for intervention. For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document duration (18 months, progressive), the specific treatments and their dates and durations (above), and concrete functional loss: **I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times a night with pain.** For the numeric pain score the guideline refers to, please see [pain rating out of 10 as recorded in Dr. Okafor's office note — date of note].

## 5. Imaging

The policy states:

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods: X-ray report or provider interpretation of x-rays that utilizes or can be correlated with the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system of osteoarthritis MRI report from a radiologist that utilizes or can be correlated with the modified Outerbridge or similar classification system related to articular cartilage injury and osteoarthritis"

and:

> "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis, or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

My **MRI of 2026-06-20** is well within 12 months of the request. It describes **full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition**, and grades the findings as **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially** — the grading system the policy itself names. Bone-on-bone articulation is one of the specific findings the policy asks imaging to address, and it is present and reported.

## 6. Other criteria in the policy

The policy also contains criteria on compartment isolation, alignment and ligament status:

> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III – IV or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4, isolated to the medial or lateral knee compartment with no degenerative changes in the opposite compartment"

> "Less than 10 degrees of fixed varus deformity for medial UKA"

> "Intact anterior cruciate ligament or documentation of stable knee examination (UKA may done with concurrent ACL reconstruction if all other criteria are met)"

My MRI grades the medial compartment at Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, which falls within the grade 3–4 range the policy describes. For the remaining details the plan may wish to confirm, please refer to the source documents rather than to any summary from me: [the MRI report's description of the opposite (lateral) compartment], [any fixed varus measurement recorded in Dr. Okafor's exam or surgical planning note], and [the ACL / knee stability findings in Dr. Okafor's examination note]. Dr. Okafor can supply these on request.

The notice denied my request specifically on conservative treatment, so these items were not the stated basis for the decision. If the reviewer intends to rely on any of them, I ask that the plan say so in writing so my surgeon can respond.

## 7. A request for clarity

I have quoted only the language of Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1) that was available to me. The policy contains further conditions and definitions that are not reproduced in this letter. Because the notice did not identify which specific criterion my records were found to fall short of, **I ask the plan to identify the exact criteria it applied and the specific documentation it found missing**, so that Dr. Okafor and I can respond to it directly.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Healthy Blue Louisiana to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-16 (reference POC-7CD7D16B79-75735) and authorize the partial knee replacement, CPT 27446, as requested by Dr. Okafor. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with training in orthopedic surgery.

If any record is missing from the file, please contact me or Dr. Okafor's office and we will provide it promptly. I understand that my appeal must be received by **2027-02-12**, and I am submitting it well before that date. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address is not correct, please let me know at the number below and I will resend it to the right place.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Novak**
Member ID: W671638429
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-16 (reference POC-7CD7D16B79-75735)
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-22 to 2026-06-28, 20 visits)
- MRI report dated 2026-06-20
- Office notes from Dr. Okafor, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records (NSAIDs; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-07)
- [Any other records you are including]
